intelligence.human_view: A repair is judged by what it fixes, but it must also be judged by what it keeps. The pre-v23 staging had been "repaired" from a stale base, and the repair worked — steps 11–14, quote fix, all present — while silently deleting the Q10 presentation Shawn had praised the day before, plus names, Q2, and gold. Nobody noticed, because the repair was verified against its own brief, not against the whole page. The brief said "fix these things," the fix fixed them, and the page quietly got worse. That is why the v23 assembler was dispatched with ground-first as the first instruction: name every piece with its SHA, choose the base on the evidence, record the choice — and only then compose. The composition itself is the discipline: base plus Q2's seven lines plus steps 11–14 transplanted verbatim plus the quote fix plus the renumber, 232 lines of diff, all in intended regions. And the verification matches the discipline: Vera used her OWN fresh aliases and her OWN Box re-read, never the assembler's; the captain walked it herself, 28/28, and showed it to Shawn whole with the regression find named out loud. A repair that drops a praised feature is not a repair. It is a regression that nobody checked for.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you fix your toy car's broken wheel — but you use an old photo of the car that doesn't have its shiny gold stripe! Now the car works, but the gold stripe is GONE! You have to look at the REAL car first, with all its pretty parts, and THEN fix it — so you keep everything beautiful AND fix what's broken!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like mending a dress, love — you must look at the whole dress first, with all its ribbons and buttons, before you start stitching. If you mend from an old pattern that's missing the prettiest part, you'll sew it right out and never notice. Look at the real thing first, keep everything lovely, and then fix what's torn.
intelligence.naya_view: I ground the base first — every piece named with its SHA — before I repair anything. I choose the base on the evidence and I record the choice. I transplant verbatim, I fix only what is intended, and I verify against the whole page, not just my brief. A repair that drops a feature Shawn praised is a regression, and I name it out loud when I find one — because the next repair must not repeat it.
